comparison: Perfect agreement on HFD1 stress response kinetics (C28-C34). Both accept the differential kinetics data showing transient vs sustained HFD1 induction across stress conditions. OpenEval notes reasonable inference about accumulating damage; peer reviewers do not challenge these findings.

Strong agreement on mitochondrial import block (C99-C118). Both accept the pre-protein accumulation data, low concentration threshold, and preserved membrane potential. OpenEval provides detailed support; peer reviewers acknowledge 'solid' evidence though note mechanism remains unclear. Peer R5 also includes C23 (overall model) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Complete agreement on structure-function relationship (C78-C85). Both accept that saturated analog t-2-hex-H2 lacks activity in reporter assays and aggregation studies, demonstrating unsaturation-dependent mechanism. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement on transcriptomic findings (C3-C64, C65-C77, C142-C143). OpenEval R2 covers RNA-seq data showing proteostatic stress response; OpenEval R3 covers promoter analysis and reporter validation. Peer R3 acknowledges transcriptomic changes affecting 1/3 of genes as a strength. High overlap on stress response genes (C42-C64) with peer review also accepting promoter analysis claims.

Divergence on mechanistic model (C165-C166, C182, C198). OpenEval finds the integrated model well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, stating 'molecular mechanism remains unclear' and 'underlying molecular modification...not yet known,' indicating the precise mechanism connecting TOM lipidation to import block is not fully resolved.

Agreement on protein aggregation and proteostatic crisis (C86-C98). OpenEval emphasizes Hsp104-GFP data, proteasome inhibition, and cycloheximide dependence. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'impairment of mitochondrial protein biogenesis' without challenging aggregation findings. Peer R4 includes additional claims C6-C7 not in OpenEval R5.

Agreement on Hfd1 protective role (C2, C27, C35-C41). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from growth assays and functional characterization. Peer reviewers accept Hfd1 as 'detoxifying enzyme' without challenge. Peer R2 includes additional lipidation claims (C144-C149, C188-C190) and gene dose effects (C21-C22) that OpenEval addresses in other results.

Agreement on TOM complex targeting (C18, C144-C158). OpenEval details co-IP, chemoproteomics, and alkyne labeling evidence. Peer reviewers affirm TOM targeting is supported by 'solid evidence.' Peer R1 includes additional claims about Tom40 mutants and tom20Δ/tom70Δ effects (C19-C20, C159-C164) that OpenEval addresses in R10.

Agreement on TOM complex mutant analysis (C19-C22, C159-C164). OpenEval emphasizes that Tom40CFREE lacks resistance despite in vitro lipidation, and protective effects of tom20Δ/tom70Δ. Peer R1 encompasses these claims as part of overall TOM targeting evidence, affirming findings are 'solid.'

Agreement on SATAY genetic requirements for stress response (C10, C119-C127, C130). OpenEval highlights HSF1 essentialization and validation of PDR1/FMP52. Peer reviewers identify 'functional genomics approach' as strength without challenging SATAY findings. Peer R6 includes broader set of genetic requirements (C11-C14, C128-C129, C131-C141) that OpenEval addresses across R7, R8, and R15.

Agreement on translation/ribosome genetic requirements (C13-C14, C128-C141, C204). OpenEval emphasizes SATAY enrichment, ribosomal mutant validation, and correlation between growth rate and tolerance. Peer R6 accepts functional genomics findings. Peer R6 also includes HSF1-related claims (C10-C12, C119-C127, C130-C135) that OpenEval addresses in R7 and R15.

Agreement on translation inhibition experiments (C15-C17). OpenEval cites these as evidence that slowing protein synthesis alleviates stress. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge as part of overall evidence.

Agreement on FMP52 and PDR1 validation (C132-C135). OpenEval notes severe fmp52Δ sensitivity and speculative detoxification function. Peer R6 encompasses these as part of functional genomics approach strength. No specific concerns raised about these validation experiments.

Agreement on background/contextual claims (C167-C205 overlap). Both accept established literature on proteostasis, mitochondrial import, stress responses, and disease connections. OpenEval notes these provide appropriate conceptual framework; peer reviewers do not challenge this background information.

Agreement on literature context (C1, C25-C26). Both accept cross-species conservation of t-2-hex toxicity and mechanistic differences motivating yeast investigation. These are well-established facts from prior work accepted by both evaluations.

Agreement on SATAY-transcriptome correlation (C142-C143). OpenEval finds strong validation between genetic requirements and transcriptional responses. Peer R3 encompasses this as part of overall transcriptomic strength, acknowledging comprehensive nature of gene expression changes.

Agreement on promoter analysis and reporter assays (C65-C77). OpenEval details in silico analysis, dose-response data, and EC50 values showing preferential proteostatic pathway activation. Peer R3 accepts transcriptomic findings broadly, which includes validation of these transcriptional mechanisms.

Agreement on converging evidence for import block (C183). OpenEval emphasizes integration of biochemical, genetic, and functional data independent of membrane potential changes. Peer R5 acknowledges mitochondrial protein import is affected with 'solid' evidence, though mechanism unclear.

Peer reviewers accept reporter assay results (C8-C9) showing transcriptional activation. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these claims, though they support transcriptomic findings evaluated in OpenEval R2 and R3.

Peer reviewers accept established proteostasis knowledge (C167-C168). OpenEval R16 addresses broader background claims including these, but peer R13 specifically isolates these as uncontested established facts.
